headline: China lands a rocket booster on a ship at sea

sources.title: Making history! China lands rocket during an orbital launch for 1st time ever
China becomes second country to recover orbital booster with Long March 10B
China Successfully Launches, Retrieves Reusable Rocket Booster

chunks.text: China has {{pulled off}} a major step in [[space travel]]. From the Hainan Commercial Space Launch Site, a new rocket called the Long March-10B {{took off}}, carried a [[satellite]] into [[orbit]], and then guided its huge lower part, or [[booster]], safely back to Earth. China became only the second country, after the United States, to recover an orbital rocket so it can be used again.

chunks.text: After the rocket climbed high into the sky, its [[first stage]] separated and {{came down}} toward the sea. About six minutes later, a giant net on a [[floating platform]] caught it. Chinese engineers had {{set up}} this [[net capture]] system, and they had never {{tried out}} such a design in a real flight before.

To create or establish something new

chunks.text: Landing a booster is difficult, but it {{pays off}}. Normally, rockets are used only once and then {{thrown away}}. If the same booster can fly again and again, companies can {{cut down}} their costs and launch far more often. For years, the American company SpaceX has led this field, and China is now working hard to {{catch up}}.

chunks.text: The Long March-10B stands about 63 meters tall, and one day it may help {{carry out}} China's plan to send [[astronauts]] to the Moon. Engineers now want to {{look over}} the returned booster, and they hope to fly it again before the end of the year. If everything {{goes ahead}} as planned, [[reusable]] Chinese rockets could soon become normal.

tf.s: The Long March-10B took off and carried a satellite into orbit.
tf.why: Take off means to leave the ground and begin to fly, which the rocket did before releasing its satellite.

tf.s: China has already caught up with SpaceX and now leads the field.
tf.why: SpaceX has led for years, so China is still trying to catch up, not leading.

tf.s: After separating, the booster was thrown away into the ocean.
tf.why: The booster was caught in a net to be used again, so it was not thrown away, which means to get rid of something.

tf.s: Engineers said the landing had failed and did not pay off.
tf.why: The landing succeeded, so the effort did pay off, which means to bring a good result.

tf.s: Reusing boosters could help companies cut down their costs.
tf.why: Cut down means to reduce, and flying the same booster again cuts down launch costs.

tf.s: Chinese engineers set up a net system to catch the booster.
tf.why: Set up means to create or establish something new, which is what the engineers did with the net system.
